title: Show catalog demo failures instead of a false success
prompt:
Fix the Try It catalog demonstration on /get-started. Evidence: src/app/get-started/page.tsx:65-74 parses every response and constructs status="ok" without checking res.ok. A local execution of the actual widget with HTTP 500 and {error:true,message:"Unavailable"} displayed status="ok", zero tools, and zero providers. This tells a new developer that an unavailable API worked.

Change only src/app/get-started/page.tsx in production. Require an OK response and an object containing an array-valued tools field before constructing the success summary. Use the existing error display for unsuccessful HTTP responses, malformed payloads, invalid JSON, and rejected requests. Always release the running state so the button can be retried. Preserve the successful empty-catalog result and the populated summary, including its first-tool sample. Keep this limited to response classification; leave pagination and clipboard behavior alone.

Add exactly one new test file, tests/try-catalog-http-errors.test.ts. Use node:test, in-memory TypeScript transpilation, and lightweight React/JSX and fetch stubs to invoke the actual widget button and render its resulting state. Cover HTTP 500 with and without tools, HTTP 429, missing/non-array tools, empty success, populated success, invalid JSON, and rejection. Resolve TypeScript from the root installation or existing factory package fallback; add no dependencies. Run node --experimental-strip-types --test tests/try-catalog-http-errors.test.ts. No credentials, deploys, sends, payments, migrations, workflows, package.json, or auth changes. Do not commit or push; work on the assigned branch you are on.
